correctness.rationale: Conditioning on exponential first arrivals in the two independent residual half-chains gives A’=-alpha e^{-alpha t} B, B’=-beta e^{-beta t} A, A(0)=B(0)=1. The vertex vacancy law satisfies p(t)=A(t)B(t), not an uncontrolled mean-field factorization. Eliminating B yields A”+alpha A’-alpha beta e^{-(alpha+beta)t} A=0; the change z=2 sqrt(h) e^{-(alpha+beta)t/2} reduces it to modified Bessel order nu. Correct Bessel Wronskian initialization and limiting K_nu/I_nu series yield p(infinity)=[h/(2+h)] 0F1(;2+nu;h)0F1(;2+mu;h). At equal rates A=B=exp(e^{-alpha t}-1), so p∞=e^-2. Expanding the analytic hypergeometric factors gives epsilon/2-5epsilon²/6+O(epsilon³), independent of overall rate scale. Independently integrated cavity ODE and hypergeometric values matched in five regimes at error <1.1e-11; the infinite-chain proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: Qualified PASS for all-positive alternating two-bond-rate infinite-chain Bessel expression and sharp weak-minority asymptotic. Classical homogeneous dimer jamming e^-2 is known, as are nonuniform square-lattice orientation-rate models, imperfect sites, and bond-disorder studies. None of the compared published models is an explicit all-positive deterministic period-two bond clock law. A general inhomogeneous random-greedy matching formula could subsume the expression; no completeness claim is made.

The classical homogeneous limit is expressly not novel.
